title: Mechanical power balance under adopted wall laws

items.title: Adopted Navier friction law for a stationary wall
items.design_state: Step 1 local postulate complete; the current continuum and boundary-data inputs are both Step-1 ready.

references.title: Gui-Qiang Chen and Zhongmin Qian, A Study of the Navier-Stokes Equations with the Kinematic and Navier Boundary Conditions
references.locator: arXiv:0901.0147v1, §1 equations (1.1), (1.3)–(1.4), and §2 equation (2.5) / Proposition 2.1, PDF pp. 1–5. The paper uses slip length ζ>0 and density-normalized viscosity; with σ=−pI+2ηD the friction coefficient here is β=η/ζ.

items.physical_scope: An adopted smooth stationary impermeable wall law for the incompressible Newtonian branch; no universality, measured coefficient, roughness derivation, or moving-wall slip law is asserted.

items.title: Local momentum equation from the adopted continuum balance
items.design_state: Step 1 local balance theorem complete; exact transport, divergence and localization argument is proved on the A page from current physical and mathematical interfaces.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2
references.locator: §§3.1.1–3.1.2, PDF pp. 4–8 (printed pp. 57–61): local momentum, Cauchy stress and stress divergence.

references.title: Joseph M. Powers, Lecture Notes on Intermediate Fluid Mechanics
references.locator: §4.4.5.2, printed pp. 145–146: momentum-derived mechanical energy equation and continuum stress work.

items.physical_scope: Smooth positive-density constant-density incompressible Newtonian material regions under the adopted integral momentum balance. It derives the local forced momentum equation by transport and localization; it asserts no solution existence or empirical validity.

items.title: Mechanical power balance under adopted wall laws
items.design_state: Step 1 proof complete; the current smooth-wall uniqueness carrier, complete integrating-factor proof and readiness record match the bounded stationary use.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2
references.locator: §§3.1.1–3.1.2 and §§3.2.1–3.2.3, PDF pp. 4–14 (printed pp. 57–68): Cauchy stress, kinetic work, viscous dissipation, no-slip, Couette and Poiseuille flows.

references.title: Joseph M. Powers, Lecture Notes on Intermediate Fluid Mechanics
references.locator: §4.4.5.2, printed pp. 145–146: mechanical energy equation derived from momentum; §5.4.1, printed pp. 173–175: Newtonian shear and Couette setup.

references.title: Gui-Qiang Chen and Zhongmin Qian, A Study of the Navier-Stokes Equations with the Kinematic and Navier Boundary Conditions
references.locator: arXiv:0901.0147v1, §1 equations (1.1), (1.3)–(1.4), and §2 equation (2.5) / Proposition 2.1, PDF pp. 1–5.

items.physical_scope: Smooth incompressible Newtonian solutions of constant positive density and viscosity on a fixed bounded C2 domain, or on the stated periodic channel with no-slip physical walls. The adopted stationary Navier friction law is used only on the bounded-domain branch. It gives conditional mechanical power identities and stationary bounded-domain smooth uniqueness only; no existence or universal wall-law applicability is asserted.

items.title: Linear acoustic model prediction
items.design_state: Step 1 conditional proof complete; the current barotropic definition and global tangent-system theorem match and both are Step-1 ready.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3
references.locator: §4.4.4, printed pp. 150–152 (PDF pp. 39–42): linearized Euler and mass equations, adiabatic sound speed, wave equation and Fourier-mode dispersion.

references.title: François Golse, The Boltzmann Equation and Its Hydrodynamic Limits, Handbook of Differential Equations: Evolutionary Equations, vol. 2
references.locator: Chapter 3, §2.3, printed pp. 10–11: linearization at constant equilibrium; §7.1.2, printed pp. 81–82: Cauchy problem for the acoustic system on R3.

items.physical_scope: Exact global smooth tangent-model prediction for a positive-density, no-force barotropic Euler equilibrium at rest on a periodic three-dimensional cell, when p'(rho*)>0. No finite-amplitude error estimate or empirical applicability claim is asserted.
